title: Aurora shift passdown draft
content:
Shift summary (aurora -> dusk, 02-09)

- General: quiet start, small spike in Hosted API p95 around 02:10 UTC that auto-resolved after autoscaler added two replicas. No customer-facing incidents.
- Open incident: INF-3421 (memory growth in serving-runtime v2.3) — ongoing investigation, mitigation in place (see 'Temp mitigation' below).
- On-going tasks for next shift: keep watch on memory trends, validate PR #1289 once CI passes, run the KV-cache eviction canary at 04:00 UTC.

Notes-to-self / highlights:
- The memory growth appears correlated with long-running chat sessions that keep KV cache pinned for >30 min. Hypothesis: a leak in kv-cache eviction logic under quantized kernels.
- Repro steps are in the Jira ticket; I attached heap samples and raw 'nvidia-smi -q' snapshots.

Key metrics to watch (Grafana panels):
- hosted-api.p95_latency (threshold: >500ms) -> alert: #infra-hosted-alerts
- serving-runtime.memory.gpu_used_pct (threshold: >85% sustained 5m) -> page SRE on-call if sustained
- serving-runtime.process.rss_mb (rising trend >20% in 15m window) -> escalation path below
- kv_cache.hit_rate (should be >0.92 for steady workloads)
- autoscaler.replicas (unexpected scale events during low traffic -> investigate scaling policy)

Temp mitigation (current):
- Rolled a graceful restart policy for pods with runtime v2.3: pods with RSS > 9GB for 20m are annotated with "temp/restart:true" and an automated job restarts them in a controlled fashion. Script lives in infra/tools/restart-on-high-ram (PR linked).
- Limit long-lived chat sessions: temporary config change in gateway that forces session TTL = 45m for hosted-api routes (config key: hosted.session_max_ttl).
- If GPU memory >90% and KV cache hit_rate <0.6, scale up the pool by +1 replica and notify SRE channel.

Quick handoff checklist (please run through):
- [ ] Check INF-3421 Jira for new comments/attachments
- [ ] Confirm PR #1289 (memory cleanup) passed integration and staging smoke tests (staging cluster: staging-us-west-2)
- [ ] Look at 'memory-growth' dashboard top panel (last 6h) -> note any rising processes
- [ ] Run canary eviction test at 04:00 UTC (script: infra/canaries/kv-evict-canary.sh)
- [ ] Verify restart job hasn't restarted >3 pods in last 1h (if so, call for manual intervention)

Quick commands (for next shifter):
- tail logs for a pod: kubectl -n hosted logs -f deployment/hosted-api --since=1h\-f will stream; prefer kubectl logs -c runtime-container if multiple containers
- check pod memory: kubectl -n hosted top pods | grep runtime
- check GPU usage on node: ssh gpu-node-<n> sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv,noheader
- restart single pod gracefully: kubectl -n hosted rollout restart deployment/hosted-api --field-selector metadata.name=<pod-name> (note: graceful termination is 120s)
- run heap capture (devs only, large binary): curl -sS -X POST http://<pod-ip>:6060/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap-$(date +%s).pprof

Escalation and contacts:
- Primary on-call (SRE): Omar Singh (pager: rotate-sre-pager, slack: @omar)
- Secondary: Priya Patel (pager: rotate-sre-2, slack: @priya)
- Runtime lead (for PR/patch signoff): Daniel Park (dm.park@redwood.ai)
- Product owner (if customer impacted): Lina Guerrero (lina@redwood.ai)
- Slack channels: #infra-hosted, #sre-oncall, #serving-runtime

Known caveats / doc TODOs:
- TODO: add step-by-step for safe canary rollout of PR #1289 (I started a doc under /tmp/canary-plan.md — needs cleanup).
- Caveat: restart-on-high-ram job currently ignores pods in Dedicated pools; if INF-3421 affects Dedicated customers we must manually coordinate with account team.
- Missing: automated alert that correlates GPU memory growth with long session ids (need to add session_id dimension to metrics).

Quick triage rubric for errors:
- 5xx spikes (>=3x baseline for 5m): check logs for OOM/killed signals -> check node dmesg for OOM killer
- p95 latency spike + high replica creation: likely autoscaler tuning issue; inspect HPA event history and recent deploys
- KV cache hit_rate drop: suspect cache warmed with new model variant or eviction bug — run kv-evict-canary and consult applied-ml team

Open questions to pass on:
- Does 2.3 backport require a model compatibility matrix update? (I think yes; tagging applied-ml).
- Should we permit temporary increase of session_max_ttl for enterprise customers (requires product approval)?

Random notes / scribbles:
- If you need to repro locally: use perf/dev-images/serving-runtime:debug and run small-load-run.sh with --keep-kv for 45m.
- I left the staging heap captures at: s3://redwood-infra-dumps/staging/heap-2026-02-08-*/
- Consider adding a gauge for per-session KV size (approx computed from kv_cache.keys * avg_entry_size).

If anything noisy or confusing, ping me directly on slack (maya.t) or call Omar if it's urgent. Leaving the canary script pointer and the restart job link in linked_artifacts.

-- maya
